name: Parietal Lobe
summary: Processes touch, spatial awareness, body position, and mathematical reasoning. Contains the primary somatosensory cortex.

connections.note: Links spatial awareness with motor planning.

facts.text: Damage to the right parietal lobe can cause hemispatial neglect — the person genuinely cannot perceive the left side of their world.
The sensory homunculus maps touch sensitivity: lips and fingertips have disproportionately large representations because of their density of receptors.

detailedDescription: The parietal lobe sits behind the frontal lobe, separated by the central sulcus. Its front edge is the postcentral gyrus — the primary somatosensory cortex, processing touch, temperature, pressure, and pain. The posterior parietal cortex integrates sensory data to construct spatial awareness. Certain parietal damage causes acalculia (inability to do math) or agraphia (inability to write) despite otherwise normal intelligence.
